# Selected libuipc sources

Upstream: https://github.com/spiriMirror/libuipc
Pinned commit: `9c748a759bb9952a7aeedd59076a70591dc61d6c` (2026-09-17).

The Apache-2.0 LICENSE and upstream NOTICE are retained. These are private implementation sources, not an installed libuipc ABI. Imported headers have their includes adapted to this directory; `include/libuipc/type_define.h` is a new minimal compatibility bridge. Distance and material-math formulas are retained. The PT/EE routines in `distance/details/ccd.inl` additionally stop conservatively on nonfinite/nonpositive distances or stalled advancement, remove the unsafe near-parallel endpoint fallback, and avoid extrapolating past an already-proven safe interval. They return the last conservative lower bound on iteration exhaustion. CCD uses added geometric distance helpers: PT combines three point-to-segment candidates with the interior plane projection, and EE combines four endpoint-to-segment candidates with the interior line candidate, using cross-product parameters and handling collapsed primitives. This avoids the barrier feature classifier's intentionally positive PE distance at coplanar interior crossings. Squared-normal underflow fails closed. The EVD and inverse utilities identify MUDA provenance upstream. CCD/distance sources retain their Codim-IPC reference. PGO contact coefficients, normalized barrier, mapping and broad phase live in PGO sources. The production CUDA route now uses `src/core/contact/ipc/cuda/cudaIPCContinuousCollision.h`: PGO conservative advancement following the imported CCD design, with directed-rounding support-separation bounds, original-time pose reconstruction and explicit surface-mapping uncertainty. The approximate closest-point axes do not determine the certified distance. This replaces floating primitive-distance advancement, which could cross an exact zero during repeated near-root suffix calls. Mapping-error intervals also enlarge swept BVH bounds. The full original-chord proof continues internally to completion or uncertainty; when only a prefix can be certified, the returned Newton prefix retains a conservative 10% of the initial separation instead of approaching the barrier singularity to floating-point precision. This numerical clipping reserve does not alter full-chord certificates or the barrier law. When additive advancement exhausts its fixed budget on a clear grazing chord, PGO uses a bounded adaptive interval fallback: directed signed projection hulls of the original-time endpoint poses certify each closed time interval, using axes proposed at its midpoint. Every interval retains the original mapping-error bounds; intermediate rounded poses are never rebased into exact new inputs. Depth/work exhaustion retains only the previously certified safe prefix. This interval proof is PGO code, not an upstream libuipc algorithm.

The EE feature classifier in `distance/distance_flagged.h` uses PGO's original C-IPC near-parallel branch and relative threshold `1e-20`. Upstream's `1e-12` cutoff followed by minimum endpoint distance changed the contact law and introduced finite force jumps near that cutoff without mollification. Closest-line parameter numerators and denominator use equivalent cross-product identities to avoid subtraction of nearly equal dot-product products for nearly parallel edges. Feature selection follows `ipcDistancePrimitives.cpp::classifyEE` with more stable parameter arithmetic. PGO's own `cudaIPCGeometry.h` evaluates interior EE derivatives through the closest-point envelope and an orthogonalized Schur complement; the imported expanded derivative kernels remain available for the other features. Stable paired contact-energy changes are PGO code, using polynomial/rational primitive-distance increments and `log1p` barrier increments.
